name: Drop-Ship Descent from Launch Rig
description: The drop-ship detaches from the cargo-lock of a massive launch rig and begins its descent through the dark sky, heading toward the shadowed surface of Acheron.
related_events: Drop-ship descends from cargo-lock on launch rig

name: Emerge and Spot the Beacons
description: The spacecraft descends through the low cloud cover, breaking into clearer air beneath. As it moves forward, the dim glow of the colony's landing beacons appears ahead, faint at first, then steadily brighter through the twilight haze. The beacons stand fixed in the distance, their lights pulsing in steady rhythm, marking the first visible sign of the settlement.
related_events: Colony landing beacons become visible through twilight haze

name: Sulaco Adjusts Position in Orbit
description: The Sulaco floats in orbit around the planet, its maneuvering jets firing with a bluish glow. The jets ignite once, then twice more in quick succession, shifting the ship's position as it hovers above the cloud-covered world.
related_events: Sulaco fires maneuvering jets to adjust position in orbit

name: Bishop Ends Maneuvering Operations
description: Bishop sat in his command seat, enclosed by banks of instrumentation. He spoke into the microphone, stating that the final maneuvering operations were complete. He informed the crew they could resume their work.
related_events: Bishop concludes final maneuvering operations and announces resumption of work

name: Clamps Release, Ship Plummets
description: The hydraulic clamps whine as they release. With a sudden jolt, the ship drops.
related_events: Hydraulic clamps release and ship drops

name: Ferro Initiates Final Approach
description: The Ferro spacecraft turned onto heading 709 and activated its terminal guidance system. The crew scanned for the beacon signal, but it was not there.
related_events: Ferrol spacecraft initiates final approach to terminal guidance

name: Tractor Forges Through Volcanic Ash and Rock
description: The tractor roars across corrugated rock, plowing through soggy drifts of volcanic ash. It lurches forward over uneven ground, churning up the wet debris as it advances through the rugged terrain.
related_events: Tractor moves across rough volcanic terrain

name: Ferro and Spunkmeyer Activate the Release Sequencer
description: Ferro and Spunkmeyer run rapidly through a maze of switches. Ferro counts down—three, two, one—and on 'mark,' initiates the release sequencer.
related_events: Ferro and Spunkmeyer run through the switches
Ferro initiates release sequencer on command

name: Troopers Suit Up and Move to the Ready Line
description: The troopers strap on their bulky combat armor, interlocking the plates like football padding. They tape their wrists, pull on segmented boots, and fasten web belts, packs, and harnesses. Helmets and com-sets are secured. The cleats on their boots clack against the deck plates. Lockers slam shut. Fingers move over fastenings with a steady rhythm—click, click, click. Sergeant Apone shouts, 'Let's move it, girls! On the ready line. Let's go, let's go.' The troopers begin moving out.
related_events: Troopers prepare for deployment in combat armor
Apone orders troopers to the ready line

name: Fieldstripping Weapons and Servicing the SMART-GUN
description: Wierzbowski, Drake, and Vasquez crouched over a row of light weapons, disassembling each with practiced precision. The metallic clink of parts echoed in the space as they worked in unison. Vasquez set her completed weapon aside and turned to a larger unit—a SMART-GUN mounted on a rack. She gripped the weapon, swung it smoothly onto a work stand, and secured it in place. Using a body brace and a gyro-stabilized support arm, she began inspecting the system, her hands moving without hesitation.
related_events: Wierzbowski, Drake and Vasquez fieldstrip light weapons
Vasquez swings SMART-GUN onto work stand

name: Ferro Activates DCS as Craft Enters Turbulent Air
description: The craft shudders and lurches as it enters rough atmospheric conditions. Ferro remains icy calm and switches to DCS ranging. Spunkmeyer calls out a reading of two-four-zero, reports the flight profile as nominal, and notes increasing hull ionization.
related_events: Ferro initiates DCS ranging system
Spunkmeyer reports hull ionization and nominal profile
Spacecraft encounters rough atmospheric conditions

name: Ripley and Burke Head to the Hearing
description: The elevator doors open and Ripley steps out, already in conversation with Burke. They walk quickly down the corridor together. Ripley states that her deposition is complete and accurate. Burke acknowledges he believes her, but warns her that the hearing will include representatives from federal agencies, the interstellar commerce commission, colonial administration, and insurance companies. He advises her to stick to the facts and to remain calm and unemotional when speaking.
related_events: Ripley exits elevator while conversing with Burke
Burke advises Ripley on upcoming hearing
related_occasions: Hearing With Interstellar And Colonial Authorities

name: Crew Reacts to Sudden Acceleration
description: Apone, moving down the aisle, reaches out and grabs a handhold as the spacecraft lurches forward. Bishop, Burke, and Gorman groan, thrown by the sudden force. Ripley closes her eyes.
related_events: Apone grabs for a handhold while moving through the aisle
Bishop, Burke and Gorman react to sudden acceleration forces
Ripley closes her eyes at the point of no return

name: Lydecker Seeks Guidance on Survey Team's Claim
description: In the cluttered colony operations center, Assistant Operations Manager Lydecker catches up to Operating Manager Simpson, who is moving quickly through the busy room. Lydecker asks if Simpson remembers sending a team of wildcatters to the plateau beyond the Ilium range a few days earlier. Simpson confirms he does. Lydecker explains that a member of a small survey team is on the comm, detecting something unknown and asking whether his claim will be honored. Simpson mutters about the lack of information from Earth, how they’re told only to follow orders without explanation, and how answers take weeks to arrive. He tells Lydecker to inform the surveyor that, as far as he’s concerned, if they find something, it’s theirs.
related_events: Lydecker approaches Simpson to inquire about wildcatters sent to the plateau
Lydecker receives a call from a survey team about a potential claim
Simpson authorizes the survey team's claim rights
related_occasions: Colony Operations Center Activity

name: Van Leuwen Delivers the Board's Judgment Against Ripley
description: Van Leuwen clears his throat and addresses the room. He announces that the board of inquiry has found Warrent Officer Ellen Ripley, NOC-14672, to have acted with questionable judgment and declares her unfit to hold an ICC license as a commercial flight officer. Her license is suspended indefinitely. No criminal charges will be filed at this time. Ripley is released on her own recognizance for a six-month period of psychometric probation, during which she must undergo monthly reviews by an ICC psychiatric technician. Burke watches silently as Ripley stands, pale and composed, absorbing the decision without protest.
related_events: Board of inquiry delivers judgment against Ellen Ripley
Van Leuwen suspends Ripley's ICC flight license indefinitely
Ripley is released on own recognizance for psychometric probation
related_occasions: Icc Board Of Inquiry Hearing

name: Ripley Kicks Wall, Burke Offers Donut
description: Ripley stands beside Burke as he retrieves coffee and donuts from a vending machine. She kicks the wall sharply. 'They had their minds made up before I even went in there,' she says. 'They think I'm a head case.' Burke turns to her, smiling. 'You are a head case. Have a donut.' He holds one out toward her.
related_events: Ripley kicks the wall next to Burke
Burke retrieves coffee and donuts from vending machine
Ripley expresses frustration about being perceived as unstable
Burke offers Ripley a donut

name: Burke and Gorman Deliver News of Acheron Colony
description: Carter Burke and Lieutenant Gorman arrive at Ripley's apartment. Burke calls out to her through the door, introducing himself and Gorman, but Ripley slams the door shut without responding. Burke buzzes again and speaks through the door, telling her they need to talk. After a pause, he informs her that contact has been lost with the colony on Acheron. The door opens. Ripley looks at them, then steps aside, allowing the two men to enter.
related_events: Carter Burke and Lieutenant Gorman arrive at Ripley's apartment
Ripley initially refuses to open the door
Carter Burke informs Ripley about lost contact with the Acheron colony
Ripley acknowledges the gravity of the situation and allows entry

name: Ripley Startled by Door Buzz
description: Ripley sits at a table in the dining alcove, staring at the smoke rising from her cigarette. The room is quiet, the bed unmade, dishes in the sink. Jones the cat moves across the counter. The wallscreen plays a video with voices speaking about leaving for the colonies. Suddenly, the door buzzes. Ripley jerks upright, startled, as the sound cuts through the stillness.
related_events: Door buzzes startling Ripley
Ripley sits in silence contemplating cigarette smoke

name: Ripley Hears the Colony Announcement
description: The wallscreen plays a broadcast showing a man named Bob announcing that he and his family are leaving for the colonies to start a new life in a clean world without crime or unemployment. Ripley sits at the table in the dining alcove, wearing a robe, watching the smoke rise from her cigarette. The room is cluttered, the bed unmade, dishes in the sink. Jones the cat moves across the counter as the broadcast continues. The door buzzes, startling Ripley.
related_events: Video broadcast announces Bob's family moving to the colonies

name: Newt Watches Her Parents Board the Ship
description: Newt presses her face to the glass, fogging it with her breath as she watches her parents walk toward and enter a strange ship. Tim suddenly grabs her from behind, and she lets out a sharp shriek. 'Cheater!' he shouts.
related_events: Newt presses her face to the glass, steaming it
Newt's parents enter the strange ship

name: Tim Accuses Newt of Cheating During the Game
description: Newt has her face pressed to the glass, fogging it with her breath as she watches her parents enter the strange ship. Suddenly, Tim grabs her from behind. She lets out a sharp shriek, startled by the contact. "Cheater!" Tim shouts, his voice accusing.
related_events: Tim grabs Newt from behind
Newt shrieks in response to being grabbed
Tim accuses Newt of cheating

name: Jorden and Anne Approach the Alien Derelict
description: Jorden and Anne step down from their vehicle, wearing environment suits and carrying lights, packs, cameras, and test gear. Their breath fogs in the cold air. Anne calls out to the children, telling them to stay inside, and insists they obey. She and Jorden begin walking toward the alien spacecraft. As they near it, Anne suggests they should call in what they’ve found. Jorden replies they should wait until they know what it is. They stop at a jagged opening in the hull, darkness visible within.
related_events: Jorden and Anne exit the vehicle wearing environment suits
Anne instructs the children to remain inside

name: Jorden and Anne Approach the Derelict
description: Jorden and Anne step down onto the frozen ground, wearing environment suits and carrying lights, packs, cameras, and test gear. Their breath fogs in the cold air as they begin walking toward the alien derelict. Anne tells the others to stay inside, and they obey. As they reach the vessel, they stop at a twisted gash in its hull, beyond which lies darkness. Anne suggests calling in the discovery, but Jorden hesitates, saying they should wait until they know what they’re dealing with. Anne, uneasy, asks if they should report it as a 'big weird thing.' They stand at the threshold, motionless for a moment, looking into the blackness.
related_events: Jorden and Anne approach the alien derelict
Jorden and Anne discuss whether to report their discovery

name: Crew Questions Gorman's Experience During Turbulent Descent
description: The ship lurches violently as it hits rough atmospheric conditions. Ferro’s voice comes over the intercom, warning of chop ahead. Inside the cabin, Gorman sits pale and sweating, his eyes closed, hands rubbing nervously on his knees. Ripley watches him and asks how many drop missions he’s been on. Gorman replies thirty-eight, all simulated. When Vasquez presses him on combat drops, he hesitates—two, he says, or three including this one. Vasquez and Drake exchange glances, their expressions skeptical. Ripley turns a sharp, accusing look toward Burke.
related_events: Ferro warns crew about upcoming turbulence
Spaceship experiences violent shaking during flight
Gorman shows signs of fear and anxiety
Ripley questions Gorman's experience with drop missions
Gorman admits limited combat drop experience
Vasquez and Drake express disbelief at Gorman's inexperience
Ripley holds Burke responsible for assigning inexperienced leadership

name: Spunkmeyer Loads Missiles with Power Loader
description: Spunkmeyer sits inside a battered power loader, its hydraulic arms mirroring his hand movements as he grips the servo-controls. The machine slides beneath the drop-ship with a heavy CLANG as it positions a rack of tactical missiles. With precise motion, he lifts the ordnance into the belly nacelle, where it locks securely into place. The forklift-style claws, capable of crushing with tons of pressure, release the rack. The power loader swings out from under the ship, returning to the bustling activity of the loading bay, where troopers move across the floor and overhead arms shift cargo in constant motion.
related_events: Spunkmeyer loads tactical missiles into drop-ship using power loader
Power loader hydraulic arms move in response to operator controls
Spunkmeyer operates power loader to move under drop-ship

name: Hicks Conducts Inventory Amid Loading Bay Activity
description: The loading bay hums with activity as personnel move across the cavernous space, guiding machinery into position around the drop-ship. Overhead loading arms shift into place, and tow-mowers roll along designated paths. Inside a power loader, Spunkmeyer swings a rack of tactical missiles upward, guiding it into the ship’s belly nacelle where it locks securely. Hydraulic legs stabilize the loader as it pivots clear. Nearby, Hicks stands with an electronic manifest in hand, checking off items as the ordnance and equipment are loaded around him.
related_events: Loading bay personnel and machinery engage in intense activity
Hicks verifies inventory using electronic manifest

name: Ripley Lights a Cigarette and Makes a Decision
description: Ripley bursts into the room, gasping for air, her body drenched in sweat. She clutches her chest, struggling to catch her breath. With unsteady hands, she pulls out a cigarette and lights it, the flame trembling as it meets the tip. The smoke fills her lungs as she stares ahead, her breathing gradually steadying. She reaches for a phone console, inserts a card, and waits as the screen flickers to life. A man’s face appears, groggy and half-awake. 'That's the plan. My word on it,' he says. Ripley takes a slow drag, then presses a button, cutting off the connection. She turns to a cat sitting on the bed. 'And you,' she says, 'are staying right here.' The cat blinks, unmoving.
related_events: Ripley lights a cigarette with trembling hands after a panic episode

name: Ripley Contacts Burke and Demands the Creatures Be Destroyed
description: Ripley inserts Burke's access card into the phone console. The screen flickers, then displays Burke's face, still groggy from sleep. She leans in, her voice urgent. She demands to know if the plan is to kill the creatures—completely and permanently—not to study them or bring them back. Burke replies that destruction is the plan, and he gives her his word. Ripley takes a slow breath, then ends the call without waiting for further response. She turns to Jones, the cat, and tells him firmly that he is staying behind.
related_events: Ripley inserts Burke's access card into the phone console
Ripley confronts Burke via video call about destroying the creatures

name: Ripley Commits to the Mission
description: Ripley takes a deep, slow breath, then presses the button to end the call with Burke. She turns to Jones, the cat sitting on the bed, and tells him firmly that he is staying behind. Jones blinks, unimpressed, as she turns away.
related_events: Ripley decides to commit to the plan and cuts off communication with Burke
Ripley tells Jones the cat to stay behind

name: Ripley's Decontamination and the Crew's Reaction
description: Ripley stands in a high-pressure spray of water and hot air, her body drenched and steaming as the decontamination cycle runs. Outside the chamber, Hudson, Vasquez, and Ferro watch through the swirling vapor. Vasquez asks who the new person is. Ferro replies that she's a consultant, adding with a smirk that she was an alien once. Hudson laughs, clearly amused, and reacts with mock awe. Apone calls for them to move on, and the group turns away as the cycle continues.
related_events: Ripley undergoes decontamination in human car wash
Hudson, Vasquez, and Ferro observe Ripley's decontamination
Vasquez inquires about Ripley's identity
Ferro sarcastically describes Ripley as having been an alien
Hudson expresses surprise at Ripley's background

name: Apone Enforces Decontamination
description: After returning from outside, the team enters the decontamination area. High-pressure water jets douse them, followed by a blast of hot air. Steam swirls as Hudson, Vasquez, and Ferro watch Ripley dry off. Vasquez asks who the new person is. Ferro replies that she's a consultant, adding with sarcasm that she was once an alien. Hudson reacts with mock surprise. Apone calls out for them to keep moving, urging the team to cycle through quickly.
related_events: Apone orders team to move through decontamination cycle

name: Burke and Gorman Check Colony Communications
description: During pre-flight preparations, Burke asks if there has been any contact with the colony. Gorman responds that all communication channels are dead.
related_events: Burke inquires about communication with the colony
Gorman reports no signals from the colony

name: Ripley Observes the Drop-Ship Loading
description: Ripley watches as the drop-ship is loaded with military equipment. A six-wheeled armored personnel carrier is raised hydraulically into the ship's belly. Frost approaches with a rack of equipment, and Ripley steps aside, nodding apologetically. Moments later, Hudson drives past with a forklift, and Ripley steps back quickly to avoid the moving vehicle.
related_events: Ripley observes the drop-ship being loaded with military equipment
APC is loaded into the drop-ship via hydraulic lift
Frost moves equipment rack toward Ripley, causing her to step aside
Hudson passes with forklift, prompting Ripley to step back

name: Ripley Operates the Power Loader
description: Ripley approaches Apone and Hicks and offers to drive the loader, mentioning she has a Class Two rating. She moves to a nearby power loader in the equipment bay and presses the power switch. The machine emits a rising whine as the hydraulics engage and the loader comes to life. Ripley, strapped into the safety cage with her arms and legs connected to the servo-sensor assemblies, takes a step—the heavy machine responding with a loud boom. She rotates the wrist servos, guiding the large claws into the lifting brackets of a cargo module, then lifts it smoothly. She asks, 'Where you want it?' Hicks looks to Apone, raising an eyebrow in quiet approval.
related_events: Ripley offers to operate the power loader and reveals her Class Two rating
Ripley activates the power loader and initiates startup sequence
Ripley operates the power loader to lift a cargo module
Hicks acknowledges Ripley's skill with an appreciative gesture

name: Newt Wakes Tim Amid the Storm
description: The wind howls around the dark, motionless tractor and derelict ship. Tim is curled up in the driver's seat when Newt shakes him awake, her voice trembling as she tells him the adults have been gone a long time. Tim looks out into the night, at the wind and the empty landscape, and bites his lip. He tells her, his voice quavering, that it will be okay—that his dad knows what he's doing. Suddenly, there is a loud crash. Newt screams as the door beside her is ripped open and a dark shape lunges inside.
related_events: Newt shakes Tim awake while trying not to cry
Tim reassures Newt that everything will be okay

name: Door Ripped Open by Dark Intruder
description: The wind howled around the motionless tractor and derelict. Tim was curled up in the driver's seat when Newt shook him awake, her voice trembling. A sudden crash split the air as the door beside Newt was ripped open. She screamed, recoiling in terror. A dark shape lunged into the vehicle through the opening, vanishing inside.
related_events: A loud crash occurs and the door beside Newt is ripped open
Newt screams in response to the door being ripped open
A dark shape lunges into the vehicle through the open door

name: Anne Calls for Help as Newt Sees the Creature on Russ
description: Anne grabs the dash mike and shouts a mayday into it, calling Hadley Control for help. At the same time, Newt looks past her and sees Russ Jorden lying motionless on the ground. A grotesque, multilegged creature clings to his face, pulsing with movement. Newt begins to scream hysterically.
related_events: Anne grabs the dash mike and issues a mayday call to Hadley Control
Newt sees Russ Jorden lying on the ground with a multilegged creature on his face
Newt begins to scream hysterically upon seeing the creature on Russ Jorden's face

name: Burke and Gorman Present the Mission to Ripley
description: Burke and Gorman sit with Ripley, who paces nervously while clutching a cup of coffee. Burke suggests she return to the outer colony as an advisor for a mission to investigate a possible malfunction in the colony's transmitter. He emphasizes that the Colonial Marines will handle any danger and that she will not be required to engage in combat. Gorman adds that her safety is guaranteed. Ripley reacts with anger, refusing the offer and accusing Burke and the company of exploiting her. She recalls being mistreated after her previous encounter with the creature and says she will not go back. Burke presses further, revealing that she could be reinstated as a flight officer and have her contract renewed by the company if she agrees. He mentions knowing about her recurring nightmares, but Ripley cuts him off, shouting that the answer is no. She demands they leave. As they head for the door, Burke places a translucent card on the table and tells her to think it over.
related_events: Burke proposes Ripley serve as advisor for the mission
Gorman assures Ripley of her safety during the mission
Ripley refuses Burke's request to return to the outer colony

name: Burke Reveals Corporate Interests and Makes a Personal Offer
description: Burke tells Ripley that the corporation co-financed the colony with the Colonial Administration in exchange for mineral rights, emphasizing their growing involvement in terraforming. He mentions the company's slogan, 'Building Better Worlds,' as he shifts the conversation. Later, after Ripley refuses to return, Burke reveals he has read her psych evaluation. He brings up her recurring nightmares and soaked sheets, speaking in a quiet, intimate tone. Then, he offers her reinstatement as a flight officer, saying the company has agreed to pick up her contract—if she agrees to go on the mission. He calls it a second chance and urges her to face her fear, but Ripley shouts at him to leave. As he departs, Burke places a translucent card on the table and tells her to think about it.
related_events: Burke reveals corporate financial stake in the colony
Burke reveals he has read Ripley's psych evaluation
Burke offers Ripley reinstatement as flight officer

name: Ripley Refuses the Offer
description: Ripley shouts that her answer is no, her voice rising as she demands Burke and Gorman leave. She turns away, visibly shaken. Burke nods to Gorman, who stands and follows him toward the door. Before leaving, Burke places a translucent card on the table. The two exit, leaving Ripley alone.
related_events: Ripley angrily rejects Burke's emotional appeal
Burke leaves a translucent card on the table

name: Ripley Confronts Van Leuwen in the Corridor
description: Ripley strides out of the conference room, brushing off Burke's hand, and hurries down the corridor after Van Leuwen. She demands to know why LV-426 hasn't been checked. Van Leuwen replies that it's unnecessary—the colony, now called Acheron, has been occupied for over twenty years by terraformers who never reported any alien presence. Ripley asks who these people are. Van Leuwen explains they are planet engineers running a long-term atmospheric project, with around sixty to seventy families living there peacefully. As he steps into an elevator, Ripley blocks the door, pressing for more. Annoyed passengers glance at her. She asks how many colonists there are. Van Leuwen repeats the number. Ripley whispers, 'Sweet Jesus.' Her hand falls away as the elevator doors close.
related_events: Ripley confronts Van Leuwen in the corridor after leaving the conference room
Van Leuwen dismisses Ripley's concern about LV-426
related_occasions: Conference Room Meeting

name: Van Leuwen Reveals the Colony on Acheron
description: Ripley follows Van Leuwen down the corridor after leaving the conference room, pressing him to explain why no one will investigate LV-426. Van Leuwen tells her the planet, now called Acheron, has been home to a terraforming colony for over twenty years. He says the colony consists of sixty to seventy families who have lived there peacefully, setting up atmosphere processors to make the planet habitable. As he steps into an elevator with others, Ripley stops the door from closing to keep asking questions. An elevator passenger tells her to mind her manners. Ripley lets go of the door, her hand falling away as the doors close on her stunned expression.
related_events: Van Leuwen explains the purpose and status of the LV-426 colony to Ripley
Ripley prevents the elevator door from closing to continue questioning Van Leuwen
related_occasions: Conference Room Meeting

name: Ripley Learns of the Colonists on LV-426
description: After confronting Van Leuwen in the corridor, Ripley follows him into an elevator, demanding to know how many people are living on LV-426. Van Leuwen tells her there are sixty to seventy families—terraformers who have been on the planet for over twenty years. As the number sinks in, Ripley's hand slips from the elevator door. Annoyed, a passenger inside asks if she minds, and the doors close, leaving her standing in the hallway, motionless.
related_events: Elevator passenger expresses annoyance at Ripley's interruption
Ripley releases the elevator door upon hearing the number of colonists
related_occasions: Conference Room Meeting

name: The Arrival and Breach of the Shuttle
description: Massive metal forms descend around the silent shuttle, casting shadows in the dim light. A deep, resonant clang echoes through the hull, followed by beams of light piercing through dusty windows. From outside, two cutting torches pierce the airlock door, their flames carving through the metal with steady precision. The paths of the torches move toward each other, meeting seamlessly as the final cut is made. With a sharp clatter, the door breaks free and falls inward, revealing a multi-armed robot welder standing beyond. Three figures in bio-isolation suits step into the shuttle, their lights cutting through the darkness.
related_events: Massive metal forms descend around the shuttle
Basso profundo clang reverberates through shuttle hull
Searchlights illuminate dusty shuttle windows
Cutting torch breaches airlock door
Second cutting torch joins breach operation
Torch paths converge and cut complete

name: Discovery of Ripley in the Hypersleep Capsule
description: The airlock door collapses inward as a cutting torch finishes its path through the metal, followed by a second torch meeting it with precise symmetry. Outside, a multi-armed robot welder stands in the shadows, motionless. Three men in bio-isolation suits step into the shuttle, their lights cutting through the dust-laden air. They move toward a sarcophagus-like hypersleep capsule. The leader reaches out, wiping a patch of dust from the canopy. Light spills inside, revealing the face of a woman—Warrant Officer Ripley—lying in still repose. Nestled against her is a cat, Jone, unmoving but present. The leader checks the readouts. 'Lights are green. She's alive,' he says. 'Well, there goes our salvage, guys.'
related_events: Three men in bio-isolation suits enter shuttle
Airlock door collapses inward
Robot welder revealed outside breached airlock
Torch paths converge and cut complete
Leader's hand wipes dust from hypersleep capsule canopy
Light illuminates woman inside hypersleep capsule
Leader confirms Ripley is alive
Jone the ship's cat is discovered beside Ripley

name: Russ Jorden Finds Magnetic Anomaly, Family Debates Ownership
description: Russ Jorden sits at the controls of the tractor, focused on a pinging scope. A strong magnetic signal appears, drawing an excited cackle from him. He stares at the readout and declares the find his own. Anne corrects him, reminding him it's half hers. From the back of the vehicle, their daughter Newt shouts that it's also half hers. Russ mutters about having too many partners. Newt asks when they’ll return to town, saying she wants to play 'Monster Maze.' Her brother Tim teases her, accusing her of cheating. They bicker until Anne snaps at them to stop and warns them about playing in the air ducts. Newt protests that all the kids do it. Just then, Russ reacts in awe, uttering a hushed exclamation. Through the front canopy, a massive, bone-like structure emerges from the ash—a crashed extraterrestrial ship, half-buried and unmistakably alien.
related_events: Russ Jorden detects a strong magnetic signal while prospecting
Russ Jorden declares ownership of the magnetic find
Anne asserts her partial ownership of the find
Newt claims shared ownership of the discovery

name: Tim and Newt Argue Over Cheating in Monster Maze
description: Tim leans in close to his sister Newt, accusing her of cheating during their game of 'Monster Maze.' Newt snaps back, denying she cheats and insisting she's simply the best. Their bickering grows louder until their mother, Anne, turns around and warns them both that if she catches either of them playing in the air ducts again, they’ll be punished. Newt protests, saying all the other kids play in the ducts too, but Anne holds firm.
related_events: Tim accuses Newt of cheating in 'Monster Maze'
Newt defends her gameplay as skillful, not cheating
Anne threatens punishment for playing in air ducts
Newt justifies playing in air ducts by peer behavior

name: Russ Jorden Discovers Alien Ship After Newt Asks to Return to Town
description: Newt asks her father when they will go back to town, saying she wants to play 'Monster Maze.' Her brother Tim teases her, and their mother warns them both to stop misbehaving. Suddenly, Russ Jorden lets out a hushed exclamation, his eyes fixed on the horizon. Through the front canopy, a massive, bone-like structure rises from the ash bed—an enormous, canted shape fused against a rock outcropping by an old lava flow. The tractor slows as the crew takes in the sight: a wrecked extraterrestrial ship of nonhuman, biomechanoid design. Russ whispers in awe, 'Folks, we have scored big this time.'
related_events: Newt asks to return to town to play 'Monster Maze'
Russ Jorden discovers an extraterrestrial ship in the ash bed
The prospecting vehicle slows upon sighting the alien ship

name: Boarding the APC for Deployment
description: Ripley, wearing a flight jacket and headset, files into the ship with the troopers and enters the APC. They take seats facing each other across a narrow aisle, strapping in for rapid deployment. A klaxon sounds, signaling the depressurization of the cargo lock. Hudson paces the aisle, moving with exaggerated steps, then slaps the controls of the servo-cannon in the gun bay above. He boasts about the weapons systems until Hicks grabs him by the battle harness and pulls him into a seat. Ripley nods her thanks to Hicks. The motors whine and the craft lurches as it begins to move.
related_events: Ripley and troopers board the ship and take seats in the APC
Cargo lock depressurization signaled by klaxon
The ship begins to move as motors whine

name: Hudson's Boast and Hicks' Intervention
description: Hudson paces the narrow aisle between the seats, his movements sharp and exaggerated. He declares himself ready for combat, calling himself the ultimate badass and assuring Ripley that his squad will protect her. As he speaks, he lists the unit's weapons—tactical smart-missiles, phased-plasma pulse-rifles, RPGs, sonic electronic devices, knives, and nukes—then slaps the controls of the servo-cannon mounted in the gun bay above. The sound echoes through the cabin. Hicks reaches out, grabs Hudson by his battle harness, and pulls him into a seat. He says only, 'Save it.' Hudson complies. Ripley nods toward Hicks.

Ripley watches closely and remarks that the structures appear intact and that there is power. Gorman then directs Ferro to set down sixty meters from the telemetry mast and to remain on station after immediate dust off on his signal. Apone announces ten seconds to landing, telling the team to stay alert.

She regains her balance and moves to the control console, where Burke stands watching over Lieutenant Gorman's shoulder. Gorman operates the monitoring system, checking the status of the troopers. Screens display helmet camera feeds and bio-monitor readouts for each soldier. Gorman instructs Drake to adjust his camera, and after a brief fumble, the image stabilizes. Apone calls out for Fire-team A to gear up, announcing they have two minutes. Vasquez and Drake begin strapping on their smart-gun harnesses. On the exterior monitors, the atmospheric processing station grows larger as the ship nears. Ripley watches the station approach, silent amid the rising activity.

He notices a problem with Drake's helmet camera and instructs him to check it. Drake taps his helmet sharply with an ammo case, a known fix for the issue. name: Jones Collides with the Environmental Wall Screen
description: Sunlight streams through a stand of poplars, casting shafts of light across a verdant meadow where a bird hops among fallen leaves. Jones stalks forward, focused on the bird in the foreground. He leaps toward it—and slams into a solid surface. The illusion shatters as the scene reveals itself to be a high-resolution environmental wall screen, a continuous video loop of nature. Jones stumbles back, disoriented. Ripley, seated on a bench nearby in the atrium of Gateway Station's medical center, mutters, "Dumbshit." Around them, potted trees line the sterile space, and glass doors lead to clinical corridors in the distance.

name: Burke Informs Ripley of Her Daughter's Death
description: Burke enters the atrium of the medical center at Gateway Station, offering a brief apology for being late. Ripley, seated on a bench, asks if they have found her daughter. Burke opens his briefcase and takes out a sheet of printed paper, including a telestat photograph. He tells her that Amanda Ripley-McClaren, her daughter, died at the age of sixty-six two years earlier from cancer. He adds that she was cremated and buried at Parkside Repository in Little Chute, Wisconsin, and had no children. Ripley looks at the photograph, silent and stunned. She speaks her daughter’s childhood nickname, 'Amy,' and recalls promising to be home for her eleventh birthday. She reflects on how she never made it back in time. After a pause, she expresses regret, saying she always believed she could make things right later, but now never will. She begins to cry quietly. Burke places a hand on her arm and reminds her gently that the inquest begins at 0930 and she should not be late.

name: Ripley Learns of Her Daughter's Death
description: Sunlight filters through a stand of poplars on a high-resolution environmental wall screen, casting shifting patterns in the atrium of Gateway Station's medical center. Jones, a small figure in the foreground, stalks a bird among fallen leaves in the video loop, then leaps—only to collide with the screen. Ripley watches, seated on a bench beside unenthusiastic potted trees, her expression distant. Burke enters, slightly out of breath, carrying a briefcase. He offers a printed sheet with a telestat photo, hesitating before delivering the news. Amanda Ripley-McClaren, her daughter, died two years earlier at the age of sixty-six from cancer. She was cremated and interred in Little Chute, Wisconsin. Ripley stares at the photograph of the elderly woman, struggling to recognize the child she once knew. She whispers her daughter’s childhood nickname, 'Amy,' and recalls promising to be home for her eleventh birthday—a promise she never kept. Her voice falters as she speaks of missed chances, of always assuming there would be time later. Her breath catches. She does not sob, but tears fall silently down her face. Burke places a hand on her arm, saying nothing. After a moment, he gently reminds her the inquest begins at 0930. She nods, eyes still on the false horizon of the screen.

'The hearing convenes at 0930,' he says. 'You don't want to be late.' Ripley takes a slow breath, then nods. name: Ripley Confronts Bishop After Learning He Is a Synthetic

When Burke reveals that Bishop is a synthetic, Ripley reacts with anger, accusing him of withholding the information. Bishop apologizes and explains that modern synthetics have behavioral inhibitors that prevent them from harming humans, but Ripley remains hostile. She recalls a previous incident in which a malfunctioning android caused deaths. As Bishop offers her more cornbread, she abruptly knocks the plate from his hand, sending it across the room. 'Just stay away from me, Bishop! You got that straight?' she demands. Burke and Gorman exchange glances. At a nearby table, Wierzbowski shrugs and mutters, 'She don't like the cornbread either,' drawing quiet laughter from the other troopers.

description: In the mess hall, the troopers gather at a long table, nursing coffee as they wait for food from the AUTOCHEF. Hudson turns to Apone and asks for details about the mission. Apone, leaning back with a dry look, replies that it's a rescue operation to save some colonists' daughters from virginity. The troopers chuckle. Spunkmeyer pokes at his plate and grimaces, calling the food crap. Wierzbowski examines it and says it's cornbread. He grins and adds that he wouldn't mind getting some Arcturan poontang again, recalling the time they were stationed there. description: The troopers gather at one long table, their fatigues customized with patches and slogans—Drake wearing a vest stenciled with 'Eat the apple and fuck the Corps,' others displaying 'Peace Through Superior Firepower' and 'I've Served My Time in Hell: Cetti Epsilon NC-104.' They drink coffee, waiting for eggs from the AUTOCHEF, joking among themselves. Hudson asks Apone about the mission, and Apone replies it's a rescue op, joking about saving colonists' daughters from virginity. Spunkmeyer complains about the food, Wierzbowski guesses it's cornbread and reminisces about Arcturan women. Hicks notes in a low voice that the new lieutenant isn't sitting with them, and Wierzbowski mutters that he must have a corn cob up his ass. At the other table, Gorman sits stiffly in perfect uniform. Bishop takes a seat beside Ripley, but she immediately gets up and moves to the far end. Bishop says he's sorry she feels that way about synthetics. Ripley turns to Burke, accusing, demanding to know why he didn't tell her there was an android. Burke says it didn't occur to him—it's standard policy. Bishop adds that he prefers the term 'artificial person,' and asks if there's a problem. Burke explains a synthetic malfunctioned on her last trip, resulting in deaths. Bishop expresses shock and asks if it was an older model. When Burke says it was a Cyberdyne Systems 120-A/2, Bishop nods, says the A/2s were twitchy, and assures her that with current behavioral inhibitors, it's impossible for him to harm a human. He offers her more cornbread. She slams the plate from his hand, sending it across the room, and tells him to stay away. Burke and Gorman exchange glances. name: Ripley Confronts the Board of Inquiry
description: Ripley stands before eight board members seated at a long conference table, their faces stern in gray suits. A video screen behind her displays mugshots of her deceased crew—Parker, Brett, Kane, Lambert, Ash, and Dallas—as their files appear one by one. Van Leuwen questions her about the destruction of the Nostromo, emphasizing the cost of the ship. The Insurance Investigator notes the loss at forty-two million adjusted dollars. The board cites the shuttle’s flight recorder, confirming the landing on LV-426 and the self-destruct sequence, but points out there is no record of the creature Ripley describes. She insists the recorder has been tampered with and demands to know who had access. The ECA Representative dismisses her claims, stating no such life form has ever been reported and that LV-426 has no indigenous life beyond a simple virus. Ripley argues that the creature came from a derelict alien spacecraft they discovered on the planetoid, warning that thousands of eggs remain there. She grows more forceful, shouting over Van Leuwen as he attempts to end the hearing, insisting that if one creature could kill her entire crew in twelve hours, the threat must be taken seriously. When Van Leuwen stands and dismisses her, she turns away, trembling, as Dallas’s image stares back from the screen.

name: Ripley Confronts the Board with Evidence of the Derelict Ship
description: Ripley stands before the board of inquiry as they question the validity of her account. Facing skepticism, she insists the Nostromo crew discovered a derelict alien spacecraft on LV-426 after following a distress signal. She explains that the creature they encountered was not native to the planetoid but originated from the ship, which contained thousands of eggs. When the board challenges her, pointing to the lack of physical evidence and the flight recorder's silence on the creature, Ripley argues the recorder was tampered with. She reveals she ejected the alien through the airlock, destroying the only physical proof. The ECA Representative dismisses her claims, calling them implausible, especially the creature's ability to gestate inside a human host and its molecular acid blood. Undeterred, Ripley warns that the derelict ship remains on LV-426, posing a grave threat if left unchecked.

name: Ripley's Final Warning at the Inquiry Hearing
description: As the hearing drew to a close, Ripley glanced at Burke, seated silently at the far end of the table. His expression remained grim. She turned back to the board just as Van Leuwen began to dismiss her. 'That's not all, Goddamnit!' she shouted, cutting him off. 'Back on that planetoid is an alien ship, and on that ship are thousands of eggs. Thousands. Do you understand? Just one of those things killed my entire crew within twelve hours of hatching.' She fixed the members of the board with a hard stare. 'If those things get back here, that will be all. Then you can just kiss it goodbye, Jack! Just kiss it goodbye.' Without waiting for a response, she turned and walked away, her body trembling with anger and frustration. Dallas's image stared out from the video screen, unblinking, as the room fell silent behind her.

name: Gorman, Burke, and Ripley Begin the Pre-Mission Briefing
description: Gorman, Burke, and Ripley enter the armory where the marines are lounging among the racks of high-tech weaponry. At Gorman's command, the troops snap to attention. He apologizes for the lack of a prior briefing, explaining they left Gateway too quickly. When Hudson interrupts to ask if this will be another bug-hunt, Gorman grows annoyed and corrects him on Hicks' name. After clarifying the situation—that there has been no contact with the colony and a xenomorph may be involved—he gestures for Ripley to speak. She steps forward, places a set of recording diskettes on the table, and begins to explain the creature's life cycle, describing how the first form attaches to a host and implants an embryo before dying. As she struggles to describe the emergence of the second form, Vasquez interrupts, stating she only needs to know where the creatures are, then mimics shooting one. Hudson makes a joke at Hicks' expense, which draws a sharp rebuke from Ripley. Burke instructs the marines to review the recordings Ripley prepared. Gorman then resumes control, outlining the schedule for tactical database integration, ordnance loading, weapons checks, and drop-ship preparations, assigning deadlines as the marines react with groans.

The row of stasis units hums as the troopers emerge—wearing only shorts and dog tags. They move stiffly toward a bank of lockers. Hudson complains about the cold floor. name: Ripley Awakens on Gateway Station
description: Ripley lies in a medical bed, her face pale and weak, as a female med-tech raises the backrest. Around her, white medical equipment hums quietly. The med-tech flips a switch, and with a soft mechanical whir, a motorized shield slides into the ceiling, opening the viewport. Harsh light floods the room, revealing the sprawling modular habitats of Gateway Station and, beyond them, the curved blue expanse of Earth floating in the blackness of high orbit. The med-tech asks how she’s feeling. Ripley replies weakly that she feels terrible. The med-tech notes it’s an improvement over the day before and asks if she’s up for a visitor. Ripley shrugs. The door opens, and a man enters carrying a large orange cat. Ripley reaches out immediately, pulling the cat to her. She holds it tightly, murmuring to it in a soft, broken voice. The man introduces himself as Carter Burke, a company representative, and takes a seat beside the bed. He tells her the disorientation and weakness should pass soon, likely side effects of the long hypersleep. When Ripley presses him for how long she was adrift, he hesitates, then tells her fifty-seven years. She stares, stunned. Her breath catches. Suddenly, she coughs violently, clutching her chest.
